hints: Recall the power formula connecting driving force, power, and velocity: $P = F_{\text{D}} \times v$.
Substitute $P = 6000\text{ W}$ and $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to calculate the forward driving force of the car.
Since the car and trailer travel at constant speed, acceleration is zero, so the driving force equals the sum of all resistances: $F_{\text{D}} = R + 80$.
walkthrough:
State the formula connecting mechanical power, driving force, and velocity:
$$P = F_{\text{D}} v$$
Rearrange for the driving force $F_{\text{D}}$:
$$F_{\text{D}} = \frac{P}{v}$$
Substitute $P = 6000\text{ W}$ and $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_{\text{D}} = \frac{6000}{20} = 300\text{ N}$$

State Newton's second law for the whole connected system along the horizontal road:
$$F_{\text{net}} = m_{\text{total}} a$$
Because the vehicle moves at a constant speed of $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the acceleration is zero ($a = 0$):
$$F_{\text{net}} = 0$$

Write the net horizontal force on the combined system consisting of forward driving force and opposing resistances:
$$F_{\text{D}} - R_{\text{car}} - R_{\text{trailer}} = 0$$
Substitute $F_{\text{D}} = 300\text{ N}$ and $R_{\text{trailer}} = 80\text{ N}$:
$$300 - R - 80 = 0$$
$$220 - R = 0$$
$$R = 220\text{ N}$$
Thus the resistance force on the car is $220\text{ N}$.

hints: Calculate the new driving force of the car engine at speed $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ using $F_{\text{D}} = \frac{P}{v}$ with $P = 12\,500\text{ W}$.
Apply Newton's second law, $F_{\text{net}} = ma$, to the entire car-and-trailer system to find the acceleration $a$ without internal tension.
Apply Newton's second law to the trailer alone: $T - 80 = 300a$.
Substitute the acceleration $a$ into the trailer equation to solve for the tension $T$ in the rod.
walkthrough:
Calculate the new driving force exerted by the engine when the power is increased to $12\,500\text{ W}$ and speed is $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_{\text{D}} = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{12\,500}{25} = 500\text{ N}$$

Write the equation of motion for the combined system of car and trailer using Newton's second law:
$$F_{\text{net}} = m_{\text{total}} a$$
The total mass is:
$$m_{\text{total}} = 1500 + 300 = 1800\text{ kg}$$
The forward force is $F_{\text{D}} = 500\text{ N}$, and the total opposing resistances are $R + 80 = 220 + 80 = 300\text{ N}$:
$$500 - 300 = 1800a$$
$$200 = 1800a$$

Divide both sides by $1800$ to obtain the acceleration:
$$a = \frac{200}{1800} = \frac{1}{9} \approx 0.111\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Write the equation of motion for the trailer alone to find the tension $T$ in the connecting rod. The forward force on the trailer is the tension $T$, and the backward resistance is $80\text{ N}$:
$$T - 80 = m_{\text{trailer}} a$$
Substitute $m_{\text{trailer}} = 300\text{ kg}$ and $a = \frac{1}{9}\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$T - 80 = 300 \times \frac{1}{9}$$
$$T - 80 = \frac{100}{3}$$

Add $80$ to both sides to find $T$:
$$T = 80 + \frac{100}{3} = \frac{240 + 100}{3} = \frac{340}{3} \approx 113.33\text{ N} \approx 113\text{ N}$$
Thus the acceleration is $0.111\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and the tension in the rod is $113\text{ N}$.
